question: Texas Instruments Software Engineer (New Grad) on-campus technical round. The question: **Explain endianness of a machine and write a C program to detect whether your machine is little or big endian.** Follow-up: given a **32-bit hexadecimal address**, add code to the previous program to read the **content at that address**.
lookingFor: Knowing what byte order is and why it matters (networking, file formats, hardware).
Correct use of pointers and casting to inspect memory bytes.
Awareness of undefined behaviour and the dangers of reading arbitrary addresses.
Handling the follow-up carefully with the right types.
followUps: How would you convert a 32-bit value between byte orders?
What happens if you read an unmapped address on Linux?
Why does network byte order use big-endian?
What does alignment mean and what happens on an unaligned access?
